user.title: Set up HomeWizard Realtime Push
user.description: Enter the IP address of your HomeWizard P1 meter. It needs firmware 6 or newer (API v2).

data_description.ip_address: The IP address of the P1 meter, as shown in the HomeWizard app or your router.

discovery_confirm.title: HomeWizard P1 meter found
discovery_confirm.description: Set up {name} at {host} for realtime updates? This runs next to the official HomeWizard integration and does not replace it.

authorize.title: Press the button on your P1 meter
authorize.description: Press the button on the P1 meter once, then select Submit. Home Assistant waits up to {wait}s for the press and then gets its own access token from the meter.

reauth_confirm.title: New access token needed
reauth_confirm.description: The P1 meter no longer accepts the stored token, for example because it was removed in the HomeWizard app. Select Submit to request a new one; you will need to press the button on the meter.

reconfigure.title: Change the IP address
reconfigure.description: Enter the new IP address of the same P1 meter. The stored token is reused.

data_description.ip_address: The new IP address of the P1 meter.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach a HomeWizard device with API v2 at this address. Check the IP address and that the device is online.
error.button_not_pressed: No button press was detected in time. Press the button on the P1 meter and select Submit again.
error.token_rejected: The device at this address does not accept the stored token. Is it the same P1 meter?

abort.firmware_too_old: This device only supports the old v1 API. Update the P1 meter to firmware 6 or newer, or use the official HomeWizard integration.
abort.invalid_discovery_parameters: The discovered device did not report a product type and serial number.
abort.not_p1_meter: This integration supports the HomeWizard P1 meter only. Use the official HomeWizard integration for other devices.
abort.wrong_device: This is a different P1 meter than the one that was set up.

init.title: Update speed
init.description: How often power is updated. Faster gives a fresher reading, but costs more CPU and database storage. If Home Assistant can't keep up or the connection falters, the speed temporarily steps down (to 5s at most) and recovers automatically. Changes apply immediately; no restart needed.

data_description.update_speed: Realtime follows your meter: about 1s on a DSMR 5 meter, 10s on older meters. See the README for storage estimates.

cannot_connect.message: Can't reach the P1 meter at {host}.

token_rejected.message: The P1 meter rejected the access token.

no_data.title: No measurements from {name}
no_data.description:
The P1 meter has sent no measurements for at least {minutes} minutes, and its realtime entities are unavailable. Anything that controls a home battery or load from these entities is working without grid data.

Check that the meter is powered and online in the HomeWizard app, and that Home Assistant can reach it on the network. This message disappears by itself when measurements return.

polling_fallback.title: {name} is not pushing measurements
polling_fallback.description:
For at least {minutes} minutes the WebSocket to the P1 meter has not worked, so the integration polls the meter over HTTPS instead. Values still arrive, but less efficiently.

Restarting the meter usually helps. If it keeps happening, open an issue on GitHub with the diagnostics and debug logs. This message disappears by itself when the WebSocket works again.

throttled.title: {name} updates slower than configured
throttled.description:
For at least {minutes} minutes the integration has updated slower than the update speed you chose, because Home Assistant is busy, measurements arrive late, or the connection keeps dropping. The *Current update interval* entity shows the reason.

Look for heavy automations or integrations, or choose a slower update speed. This message disappears by itself when the configured speed is reached again.
